source_rules.name: Demo identity and ownership
source_rules.risk: Unauthorized creation, reading or status change
source_rules.contract: Known X-Demo-Actor identifies a synthetic actor; it is a simulation, not authentication. Only customers may submit and only for their fixture member. Customers may read their own claims; adjuster, finance and auditor may read all. Only adjusters approve; only finance actors pay. Unknown actors and forbidden operations return HTTP 403 without state changes.

source_rules.name: Submission and duplicate identity
source_rules.risk: Duplicate claims or invalid stored records
source_rules.contract: Require claim_id, member_id, service, amount_cents; optionally in_network, authorized, formulary. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII letters/digits/hyphen/underscore, 3–48 characters, beginning with a letter or digit. Policy and active status come from member fixtures. Validate HC rules before saving. A coverage denial is HTTP 422 and stores nothing. A successful evaluation creates submitted revision 1, HTTP 201. An existing claim ID conflicts globally with HTTP 409 DUPLICATE_CLAIM. A rejected ID can be corrected and reused.

source_rules.name: Ordered claim lifecycle
source_rules.risk: Skipping approval, repeating an action, or invalid transitions
source_rules.contract: Allowed transitions are submitted to approved by an adjuster, then approved to paid by finance. All other state transitions return HTTP 409 INVALID_TRANSITION. Only approved and paid are valid target names; malformed targets return HTTP 400. Wrong-role actions return 403 before checking the current status. Successful actions increment revision once; failed actions preserve status and revision.

source_rules.name: Simulated payment exactly once
source_rules.contract: Entering paid creates one simulated ledger row whose amount equals the stored evaluation payout, including zero payout. A unique claim_id in the ledger prevents a second entry. No real money moves. Replaying paid returns 409 and leaves the original ledger entry unchanged. Status, ledger and event changes commit atomically.

source_rules.name: Event and provenance evidence
source_rules.risk: Unexplained state changes or losing the evaluated contract
source_rules.contract: Each successful submission or transition appends one ordered event with actor, timestamp, from/to status, rule and revision. Failed actions append no success event. The stored evaluation and normalized request remain unchanged after approval/payment. Evidence exports include the claim, ordered events, ledger row and workflow contract hash. Local history is not tamper-proof.
